consensus_strengths: ForkAudit clearly distinguishes mutable recurrent-state isolation from output agreement and separates logical, allocator, and service-capacity memory denominators.
The four-cell ownership factorial, phase-aware range witnesses, and 288 adjacent-fan-out comparisons provide coherent receipt-level evidence within the declared sequential Qwen configuration.

The manuscript is unusually candid about evidence boundaries: relational equality, selected captured-input numerical oracles, and targeted fault gates are not presented as equivalent or exhaustive assurance.
Presentation is generally strong: the contract, cohort authorization, memory denominators, and limitations are explicit and easy to locate.
consensus_weaknesses: The reported run lacks terminal source-tree closure; compiled Triton binary and autotuning identities are also absent. Therefore receipt replay establishes captured-receipt consistency, not a fully bound executable provenance claim or independent producer recapture.

The primary audit is confined to one model and sequential one-stream execution. It does not test concurrent or scheduler-managed execution, ragged/continuous batching, cancellation/eviction interleavings, or broader geometries.

Independent numerical support is deliberately selected and conditional on captured inputs; it does not cover upstream activation construction, all recurrent layers, or end-to-end model semantics. Targeted mutations establish intended-gate reachability, not detector completeness.

The contextual deployment and serving tables are appropriately disclaimed but remain aggregate and visually prominent; per-workload variability and protocol detail are insufficient to support robust quality or performance interpretation.

material_disagreements.topic: Whether the carefully scoped receipt-level contribution currently clears the ICLR threshold
positions: R22-TERRA-PDF-A and R22-TERRA-PDF-B rate the paper 6 because the stated conditional ownership-audit result remains meaningful despite incomplete provenance and limited operational coverage.

R22-TERRA-PDF-C rates the paper 4 because unclosed executable identity, no independent recapture, and lack of concurrent-serving evidence leave the central audit assurance and practical significance insufficiently established.
material_disagreements.recommended_resolution: Do not treat the two 6 ratings as removing the 4-rating concern. Preserve the conditional receipt-level claim now, but obtain a closed executable identity with independent recapture and evidence in at least one scheduler-managed regime before representing the work as a stronger implementation audit or broadly useful serving validation.

material_disagreements.topic: Whether performance-context reporting needs new evidence or only clearer framing
positions: R22-TERRA-PDF-A requests per-workload outcomes, dispersion, prompts, and scoring details to assess the Table 2 tradeoff.
R22-TERRA-PDF-B treats the table primarily as a presentation risk because the manuscript already limits it to context.
material_disagreements.recommended_resolution: Retain the contextual table only with explicit visual separation; disclose per-workload and trial-level summaries if performance-context claims remain. Otherwise remove or substantially compress the table rather than implying that it validates ForkAudit.

unsupported_reviewer_claims.reason: The omitted upstream and end-to-end paths are real limits, but the PDF explicitly confines its numerical claims to selected captured-input checks and says they are not end-to-end verification. Their absence cannot be treated as a contradiction of that bounded claim.

Failure to test concurrent serving is a supported limitation on practical generality, not evidence that the stated sequential, one-stack lifecycle witnesses are unsound. It warrants either new experiments or continued claim narrowing.

The request for an additional model/runtime sweep would strengthen generality, but it is not required to validate the paper's explicitly single-stack case-study result. It should not be framed as a demonstrated flaw in that bounded result.

prioritized_actions.description: Release a terminally closed, immutable source/environment/build manifest for the reported primary run, including executable command provenance and compiled-kernel/autotuning identity where feasible; perform and report an independent clean recapture or replay from that package. If independent recapture cannot be supplied, narrow every affected framing from implementation audit to captured-receipt consistency audit.
prioritized_actions.verification_criterion: An independent evaluator can reconstruct the declared environment, regenerate at least one primary receipt bundle, and recover the registered identity, lifecycle, semantic, oracle, and aggregate predicates without relying on an unbound source tree.

prioritized_actions.description: After freezing executable provenance, run the same ownership predicates in at least one concurrent or scheduler-managed hybrid regime with forced interleavings, cancellation/reclamation, and varied prefix/page geometry; include a preregistered held-out fault set whose gate mapping was not chosen after observing outcomes. Report failures as well as passes. If this cannot be run, further limit the contribution to a sequential case-study audit and remove broader serving implications.
prioritized_actions.verification_criterion: New receipt bundles replay successfully under the added regime, and a held-out fault campaign reports detection outcomes and localization for production-path faults rather than only tailored positive controls or injected sentinels.

prioritized_actions.description: Audit the abstract, introduction, contribution list, results headings, and conclusion so that the strongest claim is consistently a conditional receipt-level ownership witness for one sequential frozen stack. State adjacent to each relevant result that relational equality cannot rule out common-mode defects, selected oracles are not end-to-end validation, and targeted mutations are not a detection-rate estimate.
prioritized_actions.verification_criterion: A reader can identify the supported claim and all excluded guarantees from the abstract, Figure 3, Table 5, and conclusion without consulting the appendices.

prioritized_actions.description: Visually separate or compress the contextual deployment and serving tables, clearly retain the caveated Q16 row as non-evidentiary context, and add per-workload outcomes, variability, prompts, scoring, and the distinction between timing repeats and workload units if the quality-state-latency discussion remains.
prioritized_actions.verification_criterion: Captions and local text alone make clear that no speed, capacity, broad quality, or ownership claim depends on the contextual cohorts; retained aggregate values are reproducible from disclosed summaries.

must_resolve_before_accept: A closed executable/build provenance chain and independent recapture or replay for the primary audit, or an unambiguous narrowing that abandons stronger provenance claims.
Evidence that the ownership witness and fault gates remain informative under at least one relevant concurrent or scheduler-managed regime, or removal of practical hybrid-serving generality claims.
A held-out fault assessment and clearer separation of selected numerical checks, relational agreement, and targeted positive controls from end-to-end or detector-completeness claims.
score_gaming_suggestions_to_reject: Do not relabel current receipt replay as independent reproduction without a closed executable identity and a newly produced receipt bundle.

Do not claim concurrent-serving safety, production capacity, broad model generality, or end-to-end correctness from the sequential factorial, selected captured-input oracles, or cache-off/on controls.
Do not treat nine tailored live mutations as a detection-rate estimate or suppress the M8 injected-sentinel limitation.
Do not use aggregate contextual F1 and timing rows as evidence that validates the ownership contract or establishes a general performance frontier.
decision_rationale: The panel agrees that the manuscript makes a clear, potentially useful, and honestly bounded contribution: a phase-aware receipt contract with coherent lifecycle evidence for hybrid KV and recurrent state in one frozen sequential stack. This supports a marginally above-threshold 6 for the limited claim, and the current evidence ceiling is also 6. However, the 4-rating dissent is material, not an outlier to average away: incomplete source/build closure and lack of independent recapture materially weaken a paper centered on auditability, while omitted concurrent scheduling and held-out fault evidence limit practical significance. Acceptance as a stronger systems-validation paper requires new evidence rather than prose alone.
